en.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in hidden debt
en.summary: Anthropic has filed IPO prospectus documents, and Bloomberg reports the company plans to take on nearly $900 billion in debt to fund servers, buildings and power. Its balance sheet shows $117.5 billion in liabilities against $112 billion in cash, while lease obligations and off-balance-sheet commitments such as data center, power and GPU purchase agreements are not directly reflected. Anthropic plans to cover these liabilities by growing revenue and raising capital.

Weave uses connected nodes to handle image and video generation and editing, with support for branching exploration, multi-model comparison, color correction, compositing, cropping, Painter, and other editing nodes. Workflows can be packaged as Weave tools for team members to run with one click, and community tool publishing is now live.

en.summary: Alibaba announced a partnership with Apple on October 31 to integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, allowing users in China to access Qwen's text and image understanding and content generation capabilities through Siri, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence. en.summary: Philipp Schmid, citing Sundar Pichai: weeks after launching a prototype satellite, Google's Project Suncatcher successfully sent commands to orbit, powered up a TPU, ran a prompt, and received the first full response back on the ground (a haiku). These files capture a project's fixed conventions—clarifying the tech stack, run commands, code style, and operational boundaries—so you don't have to re-communicate them in every conversation, and they keep the Agent from refactoring unprompted, inventing commands, or over-engineering. The article includes ready-to-use templates for Codex and Claude Code that help stabilize Agent output, cut back-and-forth, and make code delivery controllable and stylistically consistent.

en.title: Amp responds to the idea that anyone can push to main: the @AmpCode team doesn't rely on mandatory PRs to block junk code in the AI era. Instead, it relies on small teams, skin in the game, public feedback, and shared taste. Major architecture changes can be finalized in a single Slack thread and one customer visit; as adapters get cheaper, customers use agents to fill in the last 20% themselves. Don't use hiring to avoid prioritization, don't fetishize unit tests—use videos and screenshots as evidence. Tokens aren't a cheat code; they're new infrastructure.
